projects.name: HeirsAgent
projects.summary: A game-playing agent that searches deep and still moves on time.
projects.problem: Play Heirs, a 12×12 two-player strategy game (24 pieces per side, win by capturing the opponent's Prince), strongly within a ~300-second game clock.
projects.contribution: Built the agent's search, move ordering, evaluation and time management, in C++17 with an earlier Python draft.
results: Beat the professor's agent and other students' agents
Placed top 10 in the class-wide tournament run on the professor's server

figure.caption: Search loop. Iterative deepening repeats B–E until the per-move time budget runs out.

steps.label: Move ordering
steps.note: captures first, by captured-piece value; last iteration's best move first

steps.label: Alpha-beta search
steps.note: minimax with pruning, one ply deeper each iteration

steps.label: Evaluation
steps.note: material, centrality, Baby advancement; the Prince outweighs all

steps.label: Time check
steps.note: std::chrono budget with a safety reserve and a fast fallback

projects.name: DNA Sequence Alignment
projects.summary: Two classic alignment algorithms, measured for time and memory.
projects.problem: Global DNA alignment with standard dynamic programming needs O(mn) memory, which becomes the bottleneck as sequences grow.
results: Hirschberg's divide-and-conquer cut peak memory by 90.4% at m+n = 128, rising to 99.8% at m+n = 4,096
Identical optimal cost in 200 of 200 randomized differential tests

figure.caption: Peak memory at m+n = 4,096, measured with tracemalloc. Same optimal alignment cost.

projects.name: MCPProbe
projects.summary: Testing whether published defenses for AI agents hold up.
projects.problem: Published defenses against tool poisoning in MCP-based AI agents report strong results. Do they hold up when someone else tests them?
projects.contribution: With one teammate, I reimplemented MCP Guardian from its paper and tested it against MCP-Guard on the MCPTox dataset.
results: Preliminary: MCP Guardian misses tool-description attacks that don't match its regex patterns
Simply rewording a known malicious prompt is enough to evade it

figure.caption: Test path. A reworded attack passes the defense's patterns without being flagged.

steps.label: MCP Guardian
steps.note: our reimplementation of the published defense; regex-based detection

research.title: Do published agent defenses hold up?
research.text: In MCPProbe, a teammate and I reimplemented MCP Guardian from its paper and tested it on MCPTox. Early result: rewording a known attack is enough to get past it. Next, I want a hard number: detection rate on original versus reworded attacks.

research.title: Reinforcement learning for network routing
research.text: Using reinforcement learning for dynamic routing and load balancing in software-defined networks. It continues the SDN routing interest I started in undergrad.

research.title: SDN and information-centric networking
research.text: Literature reviews on routing in software-defined networks, the benefits and drawbacks of separating control from forwarding, and how information-centric networks retrieve content by name instead of by host.

research.title: Models from first principles
research.text: I implemented backpropagation and gradient descent with no ML libraries, and built a KV cache up from a bigram model, to understand what the libraries hide.

research.title: A small inference engine in C++
research.text: Planning a C++ project that extends the KV cache work into a small LLM inference engine: my own matrix multiply, multithreading, and a tokens-per-second benchmark against Python.
